body: The issue is that a single fbx animation doesn't have a Rest Pose matching the model's Rest Pose. You can fix this by exporting an animation FBX in T-pose from Blender or some DCC software and setting it as the Rest Pose. If you're using estimated solutions, enabling Fix silhouette will suffice for correction. However, if you want to handle twists accurately, the solution above is the most stable. Well, we must concede that documentation around this part of the pipeline is lacking. It should be added at some point. cc @lyuma

If animations differ, the Rest pose of imported models may vary. In Blender, Rest pose refers to the state of bones in Edit mode. You can verify that they assume a T-pose by resetting imported models to Rest pose using Reset All Bone Pose, Option `Fix silhouette` forces models into a T-pose but does not handle twists, so it may not function correctly for models with complex poses set as Rest.
